response: Yes, aspiration thrombectomy can be beneficial in patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Aspiration thrombectomy involves removing blood clots from the coronary artery using a special catheter, which can help to restore blood flow to the heart muscle. This procedure has been shown to improve outcomes in patients with acute myocardial infarction (heart attack) by reducing the size of the infarct, improving myocardial perfusion, and decreasing the risk of no-reflow phenomenon. However, the benefits of aspiration thrombectomy may vary depending on the individual patient and the specific clinical scenario, and it is typically recommended for patients with large thrombus burden or high-risk features.
